intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through the iconic towers and intricate bas-reliefs of Angkor Wat, then continue to the mysterious Bayon temple with its 216 stone faces and the jungle-engulfed Ta Prohm temple made famous by Tomb Raider.

experiences.name: Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda Visit
experiences.description: Tour the stunning Royal Palace complex and the adjacent Silver Pagoda, home to a floor made of 5,000 silver tiles and a life-sized gold Buddha encrusted with 9,584 diamonds. Stroll along the nearby Sisowath Quay riverside promenade and absorb Khmer royal history and architecture.

experiences.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and Killing Fields Tour
experiences.description: Gain a profound and sobering understanding of Cambodia's tragic recent history by visiting the S-21 Tuol Sleng prison museum followed by the Choeung Ek Killing Fields memorial. Audio guides provide deeply personal survivor accounts that bring this important history to life respectfully.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine island of Koh Rong Samloem and spend the day on Saracen Bay or Lazy Beach, featuring crystal-clear turquoise waters, powdery white sand, and vibrant coral reefs perfect for snorkeling. Enjoy fresh seafood at a beachside shack and witness bioluminescent plankton after dark.

experiences.name: Phsar Thmei Central Market Food and Culture Walk
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Art Deco Central Market dome and dive into Cambodia's vibrant street food scene. Sample local delicacies including num banh chok (Khmer noodles), lok lak beef, fresh tropical fruit, and sugarcane juice while browsing stalls selling silk scarves, silver jewelry, and traditional Khmer crafts.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage. Take a budget tuk-tuk or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack from a nearby street food stall or 24-hour convenience store near the resort if hunger strikes after check-in (~$2-3 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance to avoid overcharging at night. Confirm hotel check-in details. Exchange a small amount of USD or withdraw Cambodian Riel (KHR) at the airport ATM for small expenses. USD is widely accepted in Cambodia.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a relaxed wake-up, enjoy the beachfront surroundings of the resort. Take a morning stroll along the beach to orient yourself with the local area. Explore the nearby coastal village on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local market near the beach area to pick up snacks, fresh fruit, and essentials. Spend time relaxing on the beach and acclimatizing to the Cambodian heat and humidity. Rent a bicycle (~$2-3/day) from a local shop to explore the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a beachside restaurant or local eatery for a relaxed first dinner in Cambodia. Watch the sunset over the Gulf of Thailand from the beach. Stroll along the beach promenade and enjoy the night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a nearby local café — try rice porridge (Bobor) or a simple baguette with eggs (~$2-3 USD)
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit from the market and a local noodle soup (Kuy Teav) from a street stall (~$2 USD)
meals.dinner: Grilled fresh seafood at a local beachside restaurant — try grilled squid or fish with rice (~$5-7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: November is the beginning of the dry season in Cambodia — expect warm, sunny weather ideal for beaches. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen. This is a rest and orientation day, so keep it light.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to a nearby Buddhist temple or pagoda to experience Cambodian religious culture. Observe morning monk rituals if possible (be respectful — dress modestly covering shoulders and knees). Explore the temple grounds and learn about Theravada Buddhism.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to explore the town center. Visit a local history museum or cultural center if available in the region. Browse local handicraft shops for Cambodian silk, Krama scarves, and traditional crafts without obligation to buy.
day_by_day.evening: Join a local cooking class or food tour (~$10-15 USD) to learn about Cambodian cuisine — dishes like Amok, Lok Lak, and Nom Banh Chok. Alternatively, visit a night market for street food sampling.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery baguette sandwich with pâté (French-Cambodian fusion) and iced coffee (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Rice and stir-fried vegetables with tofu or chicken at a local restaurant (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Night market street food spread — try Num Pang (Cambodian sandwich), grilled corn, and fresh coconut (~$4-5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting temples. Remove shoes before entering temple buildings. Bargaining is acceptable at markets but do so respectfully. Tuk-tuk rides within town typically cost $1-3 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby island or secluded beach by local ferry or longtail boat (~$5-10 USD round trip). Snorkel or swim in crystal-clear waters. Explore coral reefs and marine life — bring your own snorkel gear if possible or rent locally (~$3-5 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island exploration — hike through jungle trails to viewpoints offering panoramic ocean views. Pack a picnic lunch from the mainland market. Relax in a hammock under palm trees on a quiet beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland by late afternoon ferry. Shower and freshen up at the resort. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the resort and reflect on the day's adventures.

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie and toast at a beach café near the resort (~$2-3 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic — fresh baguette, bananas, and snacks from the morning market (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Khmer curry (Samlor Kari) with rice at a local restaurant near the resort (~$4-5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules the evening before. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water for the island trip. November weather should be ideal for island hopping. Watch out for sea urchins when snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — take an early morning bus or shared minivan to Phnom Penh, Cambodia's capital (~4-6 hours depending on starting location, ~$8-12 USD). Book tickets through a guesthouse or local bus company like Giant Ibis or Mekong Express for reliability.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh. Check into a budget guesthouse near the riverfront (~$8-15 USD/night). After settling in, walk along the Tonle Sap and Mekong riverfront promenade (Sisowath Quay). Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (entry ~$10 USD) — a stunning example of Khmer royal architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant riverfront area. Visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) for evening shopping and street food. Enjoy dinner at a local Khmer restaurant along the riverfront.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before bus departure — rice with fried egg from a street vendor (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside restaurant during the bus journey — rice and pork or chicken (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Amok (traditional Cambodian fish curry) at a riverside Khmer restaurant in Phnom Penh (~$5-6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets at least one day in advance. Giant Ibis and Mekong Express are reliable budget options. Store valuables securely in Phnom Penh. The Royal Palace closes at 11:00 AM and reopens at 2:00 PM — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply moving and historically important site documenting the Khmer Rouge atrocities (entry ~$5 USD). Allow 2-3 hours for a thorough visit. Consider hiring an audio guide for deeper context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (The Killing Fields) located about 15 km from the city center (~$3-4 USD tuk-tuk ride, entry ~$6 USD with audio guide). Spend 1.5-2 hours reflecting on this UNESCO-recognized memorial site.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center and decompress with a walk along the riverfront. Visit the National Museum of Cambodia (entry ~$5 USD) if it's still open, or save it for the next morning. Enjoy a quiet dinner and process the day's emotional experiences.

meals.breakfast: Khmer-style breakfast at a local café near the guesthouse — rice soup with ginger and pork (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Simple local lunch near Tuol Sleng — fried rice or noodles at a street restaurant (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at a local Khmer restaurant — Lok Lak (stir-fried beef with rice) (~$4-5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: These are emotionally heavy sites. Be respectful — no loud talking or inappropriate photos. The Killing Fields visit is highly recommended for historical understanding. Dress modestly. Stay hydrated as it can be very hot in the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia (entry ~$5 USD) — home to the world's largest collection of Khmer art and artifacts. Spend 1.5-2 hours exploring sculptures, ceramics, and ancient artifacts dating back to the Angkor period.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the bustling Russian Market (Phsar Toul Tom Poung) for local handicrafts, clothing, and souvenirs at bargain prices. Practice your bargaining skills! Afterward, visit Wat Phnom — the hilltop temple that gave Phnom Penh its name (entry ~$1 USD).
day_by_day.evening: Take an evening sunset cruise on the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers (~$5-8 USD for a shared boat tour). Watch the golden sunset over the confluence of the two rivers. Return to the riverfront for dinner.

meals.breakfast: French baguette with butter and jam plus café noir at a local bakery (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Num Banh Chok (Khmer noodles with fish gravy and fresh herbs) from a street stall near the Russian Market (~$1.50-2 USD)
meals.dinner: Fresh spring rolls and grilled river fish at a local Phnom Penh restaurant (~$5-6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining at the Russian Market is expected — start at 50% of the asking price. Keep small bills handy for market shopping. The sunset cruise is a wonderful way to end the Phnom Penh experience.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bus or train from Phnom Penh to Siem Reap (~5-6 hours by bus, ~$8-12 USD via Giant Ibis or Mekong Express). Alternatively, take the scenic train (~$7 USD) if available. Depart by 7:00 AM to maximize time in Siem Reap.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Siem Reap. Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel near Pub Street (~$8-15 USD/night). After freshening up, rent a bicycle (~$2-3/day) and ride to the Angkor Wat complex to purchase a 2-day pass (~$62 USD — excellent value for two days). Get oriented with the main entrance and surrounding moat.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Pub Street area and Old Market (Phsar Chas) for street food and local atmosphere. Watch traditional Apsara dance performance if budget allows (~$12-15 USD at local restaurants). Enjoy dinner and plan the next day's Angkor temple route.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before bus departure — fried noodles from a street stall (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Bus stop roadside restaurant — rice with chicken (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Khmer BBQ at a local restaurant near Pub Street — grill your own meats and vegetables at the table (~$6-8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book Siem Reap bus tickets in advance. Purchase the Angkor Pass at the official ticket office (not from touts). The 2-day pass ($62) is valid for any 2 days within a 7-day period — ideal for this itinerary. Bring a passport photo for the pass.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn start (4:30 AM) — hire a tuk-tuk driver (~$15-20 USD for full day) to witness the legendary sunrise over Angkor Wat. Arrive before dawn to secure a spot at the reflecting pool. After sunrise, explore the main Angkor Wat temple complex in detail — the world's largest religious monument (included in Angkor Pass).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex — visit the Bayon Temple with its iconic 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, Terrace of the Elephants, and Terrace of the Leper King. Explore Ta Prohm temple (the 'Tomb Raider' temple) where massive tree roots engulf ancient stone structures — a breathtaking sight.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town. Visit the Angkor Night Market for souvenirs and local crafts. Enjoy a foot massage at one of the many affordable spas (~$5-7 USD for 1 hour) to recover from the day's walking.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks and water the night before for the sunrise visit — granola bars and fruit (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near the temple complex — rice with grilled chicken or fish (~$3-4 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food at the Old Market — Fish Amok, spring rolls, and fresh coconut (~$4-5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes as you'll walk 8-10 km through temple complexes. Bring a hat, sunscreen, and at least 2 liters of water. Dress respectfully (shoulders and knees covered) to enter temples. Negotiate tuk-tuk price the evening before for the full day.

day_by_day.morning: Second day at Angkor — explore the lesser-visited but spectacular temples: Banteay Srei (the 'Citadel of Women' with intricate pink sandstone carvings, ~30 km from Siem Reap), Preah Khan, and Neak Pean. These quieter temples offer a more intimate experience away from the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Cambodian Landmine Museum (~$5 USD entry) — a sobering and educational experience about the landmine crisis in Cambodia and ongoing demining efforts. Afterward, explore the local artisan village of Kompong Khleang or take a boat trip on Tonle Sap Lake (~$10-15 USD) — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia — to see floating villages.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Cambodia — return to Siem Reap for a farewell dinner. Browse the Night Market for last-minute souvenirs. Reflect on the incredible history, culture, and natural beauty experienced over the 10-day journey. Pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Full Khmer breakfast at a local café — rice, eggs, and fresh fruit with iced coffee (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Picnic near the temples or local roadside restaurant — Banh Mi sandwich and fresh juice (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Siem Reap restaurant — splurge slightly on a set Khmer tasting menu (~$8-12 USD) featuring Amok, Lok Lak, and Khmer desserts

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires a tuk-tuk or motorbike as it's 30 km away — negotiate with your driver from Day 9 for a discounted second day (~$15-18 USD). The Tonle Sap boat tour is best in the morning. Confirm any departure flights or onward transportation. Budget tip: total 10-day estimated budget approximately $250-350 USD excluding flights and Angkor Pass.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the hotel bar or room service if available upon check-in

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport pickup with Aegean Bliss Resort before travel. Keep snacks handy for the journey. Exchange some USD or local Riel at the airport for initial expenses. Cambodia widely accepts USD alongside Khmer Riel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort restaurant overlooking the beachfront. Take a gentle morning stroll along the beach to orient yourself with the surroundings and enjoy the coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach town on foot or by tuk-tuk. Visit the nearest local market to pick up essentials, sample tropical fruits, and get a feel for everyday Cambodian coastal life. Browse local handicraft stalls for souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort beach terrace followed by a relaxed dinner at a nearby seafood restaurant on the waterfront. Enjoy fresh grilled fish and local Khmer dishes as your first full evening in Cambodia.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — fresh tropical fruits, eggs, Khmer rice porridge (bobor)
meals.lunch: Casual beachside café — try a Khmer fish amok or fried rice with local vegetables (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Waterfront seafood restaurant — grilled whole fish, garlic butter prawns, steamed rice (~$12–18 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a rest and orientation day. No major sightseeing required. November is the beginning of the dry season in Cambodia — expect warm, sunny weather with low humidity. Perfect beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling or kayaking session along the coast — rent equipment from the resort or a local beach operator. Explore the clear coastal waters and enjoy the marine life. Return by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby cultural or historical site accessible from the beach area. Explore a local Buddhist temple (wat) in the nearest town — observe monks, admire traditional Khmer architecture, and learn about local religious practices. Hire a tuk-tuk for the excursion.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a shower and rest. Head out for dinner at a mid-range local restaurant in town. Try traditional Khmer cuisine including lok lak (stir-fried beef) and green mango salad.

meals.breakfast: Café near the resort — baguette with pâté (French-Cambodian fusion), coffee with condensed milk (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Beachside shack — fresh coconut, spring rolls, and grilled corn (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Local Khmer restaurant in town — lok lak, green mango salad, jasmine rice (~$8–12 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting temples — cover shoulders and knees. Bring a sarong or light scarf. Remove shoes before entering temple buildings. Small donations to temple offerings are appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Sihanoukville (if staying in the Sihanoukville coastal region) or a nearby island day trip. Depart early by boat or speedboat to a quieter island such as Koh Rong Samloem or Koh Ta Kiev for pristine beaches and nature.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on the island — swim in turquoise waters, hike a short jungle trail, and relax on near-deserted white sand beaches. Enjoy the natural tranquility away from the mainland.
day_by_day.evening: Return by boat to the mainland by late afternoon/early evening. Enjoy a sunset dinner at a beachfront restaurant. Try Khmer BBQ — a fun, interactive dining experience with grilled meats and fresh vegetables.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — rice porridge, fresh fruit, coffee
meals.lunch: Island beach shack or packed lunch — grilled fish, rice, fresh pineapple (~$6–10 USD)
meals.dinner: Beachfront Khmer BBQ restaurant — assorted meats, seafood, dipping sauces, sticky rice (~$10–15 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book island boat transfers in advance through the resort or a local tour operator. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and reef-safe sunblock. Carry cash as island vendors rarely accept cards. Return boats typically run until 5:00–6:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — arrange a private taxi or shared minivan transfer from the coastal resort area to Phnom Penh (approximately 3–4 hours). Depart after breakfast. Check into a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel in Phnom Penh near the riverside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda in Phnom Penh. Marvel at the stunning Khmer architecture, the Emerald Buddha, and the Silver Pagoda floor made of 5,000 silver tiles. Stroll along the adjacent Sisowath Quay riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant riverside night scene. Walk along the Tonle Sap and Mekong riverfront. Enjoy dinner at a riverside restaurant with views of the illuminated Royal Palace.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — eggs, toast, fresh juice
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route to Phnom Penh — Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) at a local eatery (~$2–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Phnom Penh — amok trey (fish in coconut curry), beef lok lak, Angkor beer (~$10–15 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Royal Palace entry fee is approximately $10 USD. Dress code is strictly enforced — no shorts or sleeveless tops. Photography is permitted in most areas. Book Phnom Penh accommodation in advance. The riverside area (Sisowath Quay) is the most convenient base.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply moving and historically essential experience that documents the Khmer Rouge atrocities. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit with an audio guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial (approximately 15 km from the city center) — a UNESCO-recognized memorial site with a powerful audio tour. Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia to see the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Recover emotionally with a quiet evening. Explore Phnom Penh's French Quarter architecture on a gentle evening walk. Dinner at a mid-range restaurant serving both Khmer and international cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Boutique café near your hotel — French-style croissant, Cambodian iced coffee (café touk doh ko) (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Tuol Sleng — noodle dishes, rice with stir-fried vegetables (~$4–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in the BKK1 district — try Khmer red curry with chicken or vegetarian options (~$8–12 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek are emotionally intense experiences. Allow time for reflection. Entry fees: Tuol Sleng ~$5 USD, Choeung Ek ~$6 USD. Audio guides are highly recommended at both sites. The National Museum is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — take an early morning express bus or private taxi from Phnom Penh to Siem Reap (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 45 minutes by domestic flight if budget allows). Check into a mid-range guesthouse near Pub Street or the Old Market area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Siem Reap town. Visit the Old Market (Psar Chas) for local crafts, silk scarves, and spices. Stroll through the charming French colonial streets and Alley West.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your first Siem Reap evening on Pub Street — explore the lively atmosphere, street food stalls, and open-air restaurants. Try a traditional Khmer set dinner and watch a short Apsara dance performance at a local cultural restaurant.

meals.breakfast: On the road — packed snacks or stop at a roadside café
meals.lunch: Arrive in Siem Reap — lunch at a local restaurant near Old Market (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Cultural restaurant near Pub Street — Khmer set menu with Apsara dance performance (~$12–18 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets from Phnom Penh to Siem Reap in advance through Giant Ibis or Mekong Express for reliable, comfortable service (~$12–15 USD). Alternatively, domestic flights on Cambodia Angkor Air take 45 minutes (~$60–90 USD). Siem Reap is the gateway to Angkor Wat.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise experience. Depart by tuk-tuk at 5:00 AM to arrive before sunrise. Watch the sun rise over the world's largest religious monument reflected in the lotus ponds — an unforgettable experience. Explore Angkor Wat's bas-reliefs and inner galleries as the temple comes to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex — visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, the Baphuon, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Explore Ta Prohm (the 'Tomb Raider' temple) where massive tree roots engulf ancient stone ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap by late afternoon. Rest and freshen up. Enjoy a relaxing dinner followed by a traditional Khmer massage at one of the many affordable spas near Pub Street.

meals.breakfast: Early snack before sunrise — coffee and pastry from a nearby bakery or hotel
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near the temples or at a café within the Angkor Archaeological Park (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in Siem Reap — Khmer tasting platter with banana blossom salad, pork ribs, and jasmine rice (~$10–15 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Archaeological Park pass for $62 USD — valid for 3 consecutive days and covers all major temples. Hire a knowledgeable tuk-tuk driver for the day (~$15–20 USD) who can navigate the temple circuit efficiently. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen. Start very early to beat the heat and crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the outer Angkor temples — visit Banteay Srei (the 'Citadel of Women'), renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings and exceptional preservation. Located 25 km from Siem Reap, it requires a longer tuk-tuk journey but is absolutely worth it.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Preah Khan temple — a sprawling jungle temple with atmospheric corridors, stone faces, and fewer crowds than the main circuit. Continue to Neak Pean and Ta Som for quieter, equally impressive temple experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Pre Rup or Phnom Bakheng hill temple for panoramic views over the Angkor forest canopy. Return to Siem Reap for a final evening exploring the Night Market — shop for silk products, artwork, and handmade jewelry.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — rice porridge with ginger, fried egg, fresh juice (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Banteay Srei — Khmer noodles or fried rice (~$4–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Night Market food court or riverside restaurant — BBQ skewers, papaya salad, fresh spring rolls (~$8–12 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is included in the Angkor Archaeological Park pass. The road to Banteay Srei is well-paved. Negotiate your tuk-tuk driver for a full outer circuit day (~$20–25 USD). Bring insect repellent for jungle temples. Sunset spots fill up quickly — arrive 30–45 minutes early.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Siem Reap — visit the Angkor National Museum for an in-depth understanding of Khmer civilization, the Angkor Empire, and Buddhist heritage. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the galleries. Afterwards, enjoy a final stroll through the Old Market for last-minute souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a leisurely farewell lunch. Visit a local silk farm or artisan workshop on the outskirts of Siem Reap to learn about traditional Cambodian silk weaving and support local craftspeople. Return to the hotel to pack and check out.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Siem Reap International Airport for your departure flight. Reflect on an incredible 10-day journey through Cambodia's beaches, history, and culture.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — full spread with tropical fruits, eggs, Khmer coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a well-regarded Siem Reap restaurant — Khmer fish curry, mango sticky rice dessert (~$10–14 USD per person)
meals.dinner: Airport or light meal before departure — airport café or packed snacks

day_by_day.notes: Angkor National Museum entry fee is approximately $12 USD. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Arrange airport transfer through your hotel. Consider tipping your tuk-tuk drivers and hotel staff as a gesture of appreciation — this is customary and meaningful in Cambodia.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort will greet you with a welcome sign and chilled towels. Settle into your beachfront suite, enjoy a late-night welcome drink on your private terrace, and unwind to the sound of the sea.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter and tropical fruit basket prepared in-room by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Ensure the resort is pre-notified of your late arrival. Request early check-in preparation and a turndown service with a personalized welcome amenity. Keep Day 2 light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely late breakfast at the resort. Take a private guided orientation walk along the beachfront property, learning about the local coastal ecosystem. Relax with a 90-minute traditional Khmer welcome massage at the resort's luxury spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest local fishing village by private tuk-tuk. Observe traditional Khmer fishing culture, interact with local artisans, and browse handmade crafts. Return to the resort for a private sunset yoga session on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a curated sunset cocktail hour at the resort's beachfront bar. Dine under the stars on a private beach setup with personalized butler service.

meals.breakfast: Lavish à la carte breakfast at the resort's ocean-view restaurant — fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian rice porridge (borbor), eggs Benedict, and freshly pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled tiger prawns, green papaya salad, and coconut water served at your lounger
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dining experience — five-course Khmer tasting menu featuring amok fish, lok lak beef tenderloin, and mango sticky rice for dessert

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Keep pace relaxed. Confirm spa appointments and private dining reservations with the concierge in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Private chartered speedboat excursion to a secluded nearby island. Enjoy snorkeling in pristine coral reef waters with a professional guide. Explore the uninhabited shoreline with a packed luxury picnic basket prepared by the resort chef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and visit the on-site cultural center for an introductory session on Khmer history and ancient Cambodian civilization. Participate in a private Khmer cooking class led by the resort's head chef, learning to prepare traditional dishes.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private classical Apsara dance performance arranged exclusively for your group at the resort's open-air pavilion. Enjoy cocktails and canapés during the performance.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast with Cambodian pastries, fresh coconut, and cold brew coffee served on your private balcony
meals.lunch: Gourmet island picnic — chilled lobster, artisan cheeses, baguettes, tropical fruit, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Elegant dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant — pan-seared barramundi, Cambodian red curry with jasmine rice, and lemongrass crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Book the private island boat excursion and Apsara performance at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and snorkeling gear (or rent premium equipment from the resort).

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer to Siem Reap (by chartered flight or premium vehicle depending on resort location). Upon arrival, check into a pre-arranged luxury day suite or partner hotel. Begin a private guided tour of Angkor Thom, including the Bayon Temple with its iconic smiling stone faces and the Terrace of the Elephants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Angkor Archaeological Park exploration with a private expert historian guide. Visit Ta Prohm — the jungle temple made famous by its tree-root-entwined ruins — and the lesser-visited but equally stunning Banteay Kdei temple. Enjoy a private cultural briefing on the Khmer Empire's architectural legacy.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town for a curated evening on Pub Street and the Old Market area. Enjoy a private tuk-tuk tour of the illuminated city before dinner at one of Siem Reap's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh-baked croissants, Cambodian iced coffee, and tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Exclusive private lunch inside the Angkor complex at a pre-arranged shaded pavilion — cold-pressed juices, gourmet sandwiches, and Khmer spring rolls
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak or Malis Restaurant in Siem Reap — contemporary Cambodian fine dining showcasing seasonal local ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Angkor passes must be purchased in advance. A three-day Angkor pass is recommended. Wear lightweight breathable clothing and bring a wide-brim hat. Sunrise at Angkor Wat is available optionally on Day 5.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private transfer to Angkor Wat for an exclusive sunrise viewing with a private guide. Watch the sun rise over the iconic five towers reflected in the temple's moat — one of the world's most breathtaking sights. Explore Angkor Wat's inner galleries, bas-reliefs depicting Hindu mythology, and the central sanctuary with your historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the remote and rarely crowded Banteay Srei temple — a 10th-century masterpiece carved in pink sandstone with extraordinarily intricate detail. Stop at the Landmine Museum for a sobering and important cultural education on Cambodia's modern history. Enjoy a leisurely drive through the Cambodian countryside.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private sunset cocktail experience on a traditional wooden boat cruising Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Witness the floating villages and vibrant local life on the water.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast basket enjoyed at Angkor Wat — thermos of Cambodian coffee, fresh fruit, pastries, and energy bars
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant near Banteay Srei — grilled freshwater fish, Khmer noodle soup, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant or The Sugar Palm in Siem Reap — authentic Cambodian recipes passed through generations, elevated with premium ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Angkor Wat by 05:15 for the best sunrise position. Bring a light jacket as pre-dawn temperatures can be cool in November. The Tonlé Sap boat cruise should be booked through the concierge in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private chartered flight or luxury transfer back to the resort area. En route or upon arrival, stop at a local artisan workshop for a private silk-weaving demonstration — Cambodia's silk tradition dates back to the Angkor era. Purchase premium handwoven silk products directly from artisans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and enjoy a full afternoon of beach leisure. Arrange a private stand-up paddleboarding or kayaking session along the coastline. Indulge in a two-hour couples or solo spa journey at the resort spa — including a Cambodian herbal compress treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private beachside bonfire experience arranged by the resort. Enjoy live acoustic Khmer music, roasted seafood, and stargazing with a local astronomer or guided stargazing app session.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the transit hotel or in-flight catering on chartered flight
meals.lunch: Poolside light lunch at the resort — fresh ceviche, grilled corn, and cold coconut water
meals.dinner: Beachside bonfire dinner — whole grilled lobster, charcoal-grilled Cambodian beef skewers, roasted vegetables, and artisan s'mores for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return transfer or charter flight logistics the evening before. Request the bonfire and live music experience at least 24 hours in advance with the resort's activities team.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Phnom Penh (by chartered flight or premium vehicle). Begin with a deeply meaningful and historically essential visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a sobering testament to Cambodia's tragic Khmer Rouge era, guided by a private expert historian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace of Cambodia and the Silver Pagoda, home to priceless Buddhist artifacts including the Emerald Buddha and a life-size gold Buddha encrusted with 9,584 diamonds. Stroll the riverside promenade along the Tonlé Sap and Mekong rivers. Explore the National Museum of Cambodia's extraordinary collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Phnom Penh's vibrant upscale dining and nightlife scene. Take a private sunset river cruise on the Mekong before dinner at one of the capital's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or en route
meals.lunch: Lunch at Topaz Restaurant or Malis Phnom Penh — refined Cambodian and French-Khmer fusion cuisine in an elegant colonial setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khéma La Poste or Romdeng — award-winning restaurants offering elevated Cambodian cuisine with premium wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng Museum is emotionally intense — approach with respect and sensitivity. Photography is permitted in some areas. Royal Palace is closed on certain afternoons; confirm opening hours in advance. Dress modestly for all temple and palace visits.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the resort. Enjoy a late morning beach walk and a private guided nature tour of the surrounding coastal flora and fauna with a local naturalist. Learn about Cambodia's coastal biodiversity and conservation efforts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a private luxury sailing catamaran charter along the coastline. Swim in secluded bays, snorkel over vibrant reefs, and enjoy the open sea. The crew will prepare fresh seafood on board.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the catamaran as you sail back to shore. Enjoy a private in-villa dinner prepared by the resort's private chef — a fully customized menu based on your preferences.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — Cambodian congee with century egg and ginger, fresh-squeezed juices, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on the catamaran — grilled whole snapper, shrimp skewers, tropical salads, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Private in-villa chef's dinner — customized five-course menu with wine pairing, served on your private terrace overlooking the ocean

day_by_day.notes: Book the sailing catamaran charter at least two days in advance. Discuss dietary preferences and in-villa dinner menu with the resort chef the evening before for a fully personalized experience.

day_by_day.morning: Participate in a private early morning meditation and mindfulness session on the beach led by a local Buddhist monk — a deeply culturally immersive experience. Follow with a Khmer herbal steam bath and cold plunge at the resort spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby ancient coastal temple or heritage site with a private guide, learning about the intersection of Cambodian Buddhist and Hindu traditions. Visit a local market and engage in a curated cultural immersion experience — tasting street food, observing traditional crafts, and interacting with local vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cocktail hour at the resort's rooftop or beachfront bar. Reflect on the journey with a curated cocktail menu inspired by Cambodian flavors — lemongrass gin fizz, tamarind mojito, and palm sugar old fashioned.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-meditation breakfast — fresh fruit, nuts, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Post-spa brunch at the resort — eggs royale with smoked salmon, avocado toast, fresh smoothie bowls, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — chef's special degustation menu celebrating Cambodian cuisine, paired with premium wines selected by the in-house sommelier

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the monk meditation session through the resort's cultural experiences desk. This is a reflective and meaningful experience — arrive with an open mind and comfortable clothing. Begin packing and confirm departure logistics with the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk or swim. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort with ocean views. Visit the resort's gift shop for premium Cambodian souvenirs — handwoven silks, artisan ceramics, and organic Cambodian coffee and spices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spa farewell treatment — a 60-minute express rejuvenation massage to prepare for travel. Late checkout if arranged. Private luxury transfer to the airport departs at a time coordinated with your outbound flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia. Reflect on a transformative 10-day journey through ancient temples, vibrant culture, and pristine beaches. Airport lounge access arranged by the resort concierge for a comfortable pre-flight experience.

meals.breakfast: Sumptuous final breakfast at the resort — full Cambodian and Western spread, fresh tropical fruits, pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or airport — Cambodian chicken rice soup or premium airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dinner

day_by_day.notes: Confirm late checkout with the resort at least 48 hours prior. Request a personalized farewell gift or memory book from the resort — many luxury properties in Cambodia offer this as a signature touch. Ensure all purchases, especially silk and antiques, comply with customs regulations.
